comparison.boundary_specificity_improvement: v3 localizes to specific boundaries; v2 is global only

rq1_evidence.question: Does boundary-specific posture improve threat detection and prioritization over global posture?
rq1_evidence.v2_approach: Global posture per control category. One SQLi reduces validation posture for ENTIRE system.
rq1_evidence.v3_approach: Boundary-specific posture. One SQLi reduces validation posture ONLY at the affected boundary.

key_differences.v2: All threats attributed to global 'Architecture' (no boundary distinction)
key_differences.improvement: v3 identifies WHERE the weakness exists, enabling targeted remediation

key_differences.v2: Global aggregation can overgeneralize: a single finding affects system-wide posture
key_differences.v3: Boundary-specific posture: findings affect only the boundary where they were observed. Other boundaries retain full posture.
key_differences.improvement: v3 avoids false generalization of localized weaknesses to the entire system

key_differences.v2: No confidence tracking. All assessments presented with equal certainty.
key_differences.v3: Confidence tracked per layer. Single-source penalty (x0.7) applied. 0 source divergences flagged.
key_differences.improvement: v3 communicates epistemic uncertainty, supporting risk-informed decisions

key_differences.v2: Pure threshold on global posture (no architectural context considered)
key_differences.v3: Hybrid: ['rule_matched']. Rules combine posture weakness with architectural context (public-facing components, trust boundary crossings, sensitive data flows).
key_differences.improvement: v3 threats are contextually grounded — posture weakness alone is insufficient; architectural exposure must also exist

key_differences.v2: Simple severity-weighted average across all findings
key_differences.v3: Risk-averse aggregation: alpha=0.6 weighted avg + (1-alpha) worst-critical boundary. Validation worst=0.3 at tb-internal
key_differences.improvement: v3 prevents dilution of severe local risk by safe internal boundaries

methodology_notes.traceability_depth: Design-based measure (not runtime-computed). v2: finding→posture→STRIDE (2 abstractions). v3: finding→boundary_posture→fused_posture→STRIDE (4 abstractions).
methodology_notes.classification_modes: In this Juice Shop run, all v3 threats are rule_matched because architectural context (public-facing components, trust crossings, sensitive data) was strong enough to satisfy rule conditions for all triggered categories. Posture-derived mode would fire for categories where rules do not match (e.g., if no public-facing components existed for DoS, threshold-only assessment would apply).
methodology_notes.threat_count_parity: Equal threat count (5 v2, 5 v3) is expected because the same posture weaknesses trigger both engines. The improvement is in localization and confidence, not raw detection count.
methodology_notes.rq1_claim: Boundary-specific posture improves threat LOCALIZATION and REMEDIATION PRIORITIZATION over global posture. This evaluation does not claim improved raw detection recall.

limitations: Single evaluation target (Juice Shop). Generalizability to enterprise applications needs validation.
v3 primarily triggered rule-matched threats because architectural context was strong enough for all categories. A system without public-facing components would demonstrate posture-derived fallback.
Traceability depth is a design-based measure, not a runtime-computed metric.
Threat severity differences between v2 and v3 reflect different posture aggregation approaches rather than inherently better/worse detection.
The evaluation uses the same fixture findings (7 SAST + 3 DAST). Real-world Semgrep/ZAP scans would produce more findings and potentially different boundary distributions.
